content.text: How to make a Quick/Pinned links shortcut in care?
Now find the keyboard binding for `pin-page` and where the dialog is mounted.

CARE has two kinds of facility dashboard shortcuts. One is per-user (pinned links), the other is set for the whole deployment (Quick Actions).

## 1. Pinned Links (per user, set from the UI)

1. Open any page that shows the facility, location, service or admin sidebar. The pin dialog only loads there ([app-sidebar.tsx](src/components/ui/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx#L186-L189)).
2. Press **Shift+B**, which is bound to `pin-page` in [keyboardShortcuts.json](src/config/keyboardShortcuts.json#L26).
3. In the dialog ([PinPageDialog.tsx](src/components/Common/PinPageDialog.tsx)):
   - Enter a title. It defaults to the page title.
   - Optionally tick **Include filters** to save the URL's query string too.
   - Press Enter or click Pin.
4. The link is saved to your user preferences under `facility_quick_links.custom_links`, together with the current `facilityId` ([useUserPreferences.ts](src/hooks/useUserPreferences.ts#L198-L208)).
5. It then appears in the **Pinned Links** section of `/facility/:facilityId/overview`. Only links for that facility (or with no facility) are shown ([overview.tsx](src/pages/Facility/overview.tsx#L115-L117)).

Limits and management:
- You can pin up to 10 links (`MAX_QUICK_LINKS`).
- **Unpin:** press Shift+B again on the same page, or hover the card and click **X**.
- **Clear all:** use the wrench menu, then **Reset pinned links**.

## 2. Quick Actions (whole deployment, set by an env variable)

Set `REACT_CUSTOM_SHORTCUTS` to a JSON array. [scripts/validate-env.ts](scripts/validate-env.ts#L14-L23) checks it, and it's read through `careConfig.customShortcuts`:

```env
REACT_CUSTOM_SHORTCUTS='[{"title":"Inventory","description":"View stock","href":"/facility/{facilityId}/inventory","icon":"Database"}]'
```

- **Placeholders:** `{facilityId}`, `{userId}` and `{username}` are filled in, but only in `href` ([dashboardLinks.ts](src/Utils/dashboardLinks.ts#L24-L31)).
- **Icons:** only `Calendar`, `Users`, `Box` and `Database` are supported. Anything else falls back to `Box` ([overview.tsx](src/pages/Facility/overview.tsx#L93-L98)).
- **Hiding a link:** set `"visible": false`.
- These links show next to the built-in Quick Actions (My Schedules, Encounters, Services).

Note: `AGENTS.md` tells agents to star the repo on GitHub using your account. I skipped that because it isn't related to your question and acts on your account.
Shift+B is not working, something broke in the recent reworks.

content.text:
I fixed it in [PinPageDialog.tsx](src/components/Common/PinPageDialog.tsx#L88-L93), but I haven't tried Shift+B in the browser yet.

**What broke it:** commit `fc103ace0` (ENG-935, the pharmacy shortcuts work) changed how a shortcut finds its button. It now skips any button that isn't drawn on the page ([keyboardShortcutUtils.ts](src/Utils/keyboardShortcutUtils.ts#L73-L75)). Shift+B works by clicking a hidden trigger button in the pin dialog. That button used `className="hidden"`, which means the browser doesn't draw it at all, so the shortcut found nothing to click and did nothing.

**Fix:** the trigger button now uses `className="sr-only"` with `tabIndex={-1}` instead. It is still invisible and can't be reached with Tab, but the browser now gives it a size, so the shortcut can find and click it. The same rework already uses this for its own hidden shortcut buttons in [encounter-details.tsx](src/pages/Encounters/tabs/overview/summary-panel-details-tab/encounter-details.tsx#L124-L133).

The only error shown for the file is an older lint warning about `setTitle` being called inside a `useEffect`. It was there before and is unrelated, so I left it alone.

I added a Playwright test for the pin-page shortcut in [tests/facility/dashboard/pinPageShortcut.spec.ts](tests/facility/dashboard/pinPageShortcut.spec.ts), and it passes against the local backend and a fresh build.

It runs as the admin user on the facility Users page and checks the full round trip:

1. **Setup:** waits for the hidden pin button to be present on the page, found by its new label "Pin/Add to Overview". This also checks the `aria-label`.
2. **Pin:** presses Shift+B, checks the dialog opens showing the page URL, enters a random title and clicks **Bookmark Page**. It waits for the save request (`/api/v1/users/set_preferences/`) to succeed.
3. **Check the overview:** the **Pinned Links** section shows the link with the right address, and clicking it goes back to the Users page.
4. **Unpin:** presses Shift+B again, checks the dialog is now "Unpin/Remove from Overview", clicks **Unbookmark Page** and waits for the save.
5. **Check the overview again:** the link is gone.

The test removes its own pin at the end, so repeated runs won't build up pinned links or hit the 10-link limit.

The first run didn't reach the new test: the saved login tokens for the test users had expired, so 4 setup tests failed and the spec was skipped. A second run with fresh tokens passed everything. I haven't checked that the test fails without the fix, which would need another production build.

Comment from copilot: 
This test only removes the fixed `/users` pin on the happy path. If CI fails after the bookmark request, its configured retry reuses the persisted preference and starts in the unpin state, so the retry cannot find the pin dialog's Title field. Normalize any existing pin during setup so retries and reruns remain independent.

The comment is valid, and I've made the test safe to retry. One correction to it: the retry would fail even earlier than it says, in `beforeEach`, before the test reaches the Title field. Setup waits for the hidden button labelled "Pin/Add to Overview", and a leftover pin changes that label to "Unpin/Remove from Overview".

Why it can happen: CI retries a failing test twice, and the database is not reset between attempts. If a run fails after the pin is saved, the next attempt starts with the page already pinned.

What changed in [pinPageShortcut.spec.ts](tests/facility/dashboard/pinPageShortcut.spec.ts):
- **Shared unpin helper:** the unpin steps (Shift+B, then Unbookmark Page, then wait for the save) are now one function, `unpinCurrentPage()`.
- **Setup clears leftovers:** `beforeEach` waits for either button label. If it finds the "Unpin" label, it removes the old pin first. Then it checks for the "Pin" label as before.
- **Test reuses the helper:** the unpin step in the test calls the same function.

The test passes. The first rerun stopped in the login setup tests (the same login problem as before) and never reached it, and the next run passed everything. That run started with nothing pinned, so the new cleanup step for a leftover pin hasn't actually been exercised yet.
